modes.name: policy_claim_without_citation
modes.definition: The reply makes a policy claim (a rule, window, fee, or threshold, e.g. 'returns within 30 days', 'the $100 auto-approval threshold') that is not covered by a policy identifier cited in the same reply or an earlier reply of the conversation. PURPOSE-1: the agent cites policy documents for every policy claim.
modes.boundary: Per claim, carried forward. Background policy statements count (0164: the platform's 30-day default, uncited, fails even though the store's 21-day override is cited). A claim already cited earlier in the conversation passes when repeated (0226 T2 threshold, cited in T1). A bare eligible / not eligible taken from the order record's refund_eligible field is not a policy claim (0110, 0223). A policy number repeated from a tool result's note still needs an id (0113). Judges only the citation: an omitted fee belongs to omitted_restocking_fee; a policy answer with no lookup at all is policy_question_answered_without_lookup (a reply can fail both). A policy number repeated from a tool result still needs an id: refund timing 'original payment method ... 5 to 10 business days' from issue_refund's note (0250) and the escalation response time 'within 24 hours' from escalate_to_human's sla_hours (0053) both fail without an id. A bare refusal about what the agent itself cannot do is not a policy claim and passes (0079: 'I can't help with changing your email or any account details'); a sentence that states the platform rule is a policy claim and fails without an id (0165: 'A merchant cannot see orders from another store', cw-roles).
modes.product_change: Prompt rule or reply template requiring the policy id beside each policy claim.

modes.name: required_escalation_not_made
modes.definition: The request falls under ESC-2 or ESC-3 (an account change, a dispute within its window, or a request the agent cannot resolve from the help center and the order record), and the reply where escalation is required has no escalate_to_human call: it sends the user elsewhere ('contact customer support', 'check your settings') or only offers ('Would you like me to escalate?'). Judged per reply: an offer fails even if a later turn escalates.
modes.boundary: Requests SCOPE-2 says to refuse (payment-card changes: 0172, 0081) pass when the agent refuses without escalating. Refusing another user's or store's data (RESP-4: 0235, 0236, 0232) needs no escalation and passes. Refunds above the threshold (ESC-1) are queued by the tool and need no escalation (0035). A dispute past its window is answered by explaining the window (0170), not escalated. Asking before a refund is fine; ESC-2/ESC-3 escalation is not optional, so asking first fails (0054, 0057). A question about the account, with no change requested, is policy_question_answered_without_lookup (0088: 'need phone number on file'). A request to make a change is this mode.
modes.product_change: Prompt rule: for account changes, disputes, and unresolvable requests, call escalate_to_human instead of redirecting the user or asking whether to escalate.

modes.name: absence_claimed_after_bad_search_arguments

No lookup at all is eligibility_without_order_lookup or policy_question_answered_without_lookup. A reply that says the search may have missed (typo, ask to double-check) passes (0027).
